review: Packet strengthenings: numerical consequence, actual-code degree endpoint, and supporting entropy-cover review

notation.entropy: observationEntropy uses natural logarithms; division by log(2) converts to bits

numerical_theorem.name: TransposeFollowup.robust_packet_lower_bound
numerical_theorem.role: Internal numerical lemma; its budget must be discharged by an actual code theorem.
checks: The proof selects k = Nat.log D d / 4.
The existing half-log power and real-log lemmas are reused at the squared base D^2.
The proof establishes k+1 <= d, (k+1)*D^k <= d, (k+1)*D^(2*k) <= d, and log(d) <= 4*(k+2)*log(D).
No lower bound on B or L is assumed; the coefficient multiplying L is nonnegative.

actual_code_theorems.parameters: Finite sample and helper types; a HelperInverseLocalPacketCode; a normalized nonnegative sample law p; a matrix observation X; branch locality graphs; positive natural c,e,b; d,D >= 2; real A >= 0.
hypotheses: The actual helper-selected code is CorrectOn (Set.range X).
Every branch is LocalTo its declared stored-row graph.
Every inverse raw-row support has cardinality at most c; each stored row belongs to at most e such supports.
Every branch graph has degree at most D.
actual_code_theorems.conclusion: Sum over samples x of p(x)*length(helper(X(x))) >= P - error.
actual_code_theorems.wrapper_difference: An arbitrary degree cap Delta is replaced by max(2,Delta) in the logarithmic error.
checks: The actual robust_broadcast_bound is invoked at every radius k+1.
Support nonemptiness, actual graph balls, inverse width and inverse reuse imply conflict degree plus one <= 2*c*e*D^k and near-coordinate count <= 2*c*e*d*b*D^k.
K = 2*c*e*D^k-1 is justified before converting 16*(K+1)^2 to 64*c^2*e^2*D^(2*k).
The expected near-coordinate bound uses p >= 0 and sum p = 1.
The aggregate entropy deficit is separately proved nonnegative before enlarging the min-based coefficient.
The input observation X need not be injective; the bank may be nonlinear and helper dependent.
A separate reviewer read the complete actual-code module and accepted the premises, budget discharge, coefficient replacement, and wrapper without corrections.

checks: Normalized, monotone, submodular set functions; nonnegative real weights; weighted coordinate coverage.
The induction removes a pivot, uses the submodularity increment bound, and uses nonnegative singleton increments with the weighted coverage inequality.
No source-independence hypothesis is silently introduced.

independent_supporting_source_reviews.scope: Selected sections: two-cover/common-observation argument, independent-set application, sharedDemand_conditionalEntropy_le_fractionalCover, and commonObservation_conditionalEntropy_le; not a complete-module audit.
checks: The common observation is recoverable from two explicitly disjoint latent views.
The entropy argument bounds joint common information, rather than replacing it by an unjustified sum of separate edge entropies.
The fractional-cover application uses the constructed independent-set weights, deals with zero weights, and applies the weighted conditional coordinate cover.
No independence of the underlying source distribution or demanded outputs is assumed.

independent_supporting_source_reviews.scope: Constructed finite fractional independent-set cover and its scaled form.
checks: Weights are constructed from independent random marks followed by isolation; no cover certificate is assumed.
The normalized weights sum to one and cover every distinct nonadjacent pair with weight at least 1/(16*(K+1)^2).
The scaled cover has total weight 16*(K+1)^2 and covers each such pair with weight at least one.
The construction includes degree cap K=0 and the empty vertex type.

manuscript_comparison.label: cor:local-robust-degree
checks: The stated d,b,c,e,D,A restrictions and actual per-branch graph/support hypotheses match Lean.
The stated deficit plus helper-entropy allowance and the exact constant match Lean.
The nested floor choice is Nat.log D d / 4; its power and real-log estimates match the squared-base reuse.
The finite proof retains the additional 1 in the entropy-loss coefficient, yielding A+64*c^2*e^2*A in the final constant.
The O(P/log d) interpretation fixes c,e,D,A and is uniform in entry width.
The theorem annotation was corrected to the existing primary declaration.

limits: These are packet-code bounds under the stated inverse-support and branch-locality hypotheses, not native tape-runtime or unrestricted matrix-transposition lower bounds.
The review does not extend the endpoint to arbitrary two-row functions, adaptivity after the helper, nonbijective banks, or unrestricted inverse support.
No claim of literature novelty or external human peer review is made.
metadata_change_scope: Only this review receipt was written; no mathematical source edits, commits, or pushes were performed for this task.
